subject: GOBACK statement
notes: 'ERROR ... in a main program' maps to the single termination-indication capability .NET offers - a nonzero process exit code (Environment.ExitCode, flushed at the write site by the RunUnit.ExitStatus setter): ExitStatus() renders 'st.Error ? 1L : 0L' when no status VALUE is present, and the theory carries the GOBACK-specific row 'GOBACK WITH ERROR.' -> 1. The 2023-only edition scope is the STATUS/ERROR phrase's own introduction gate (goback-status-2023 in ConstructRegistry). NAMED, not hidden: GR7 and GR10 collide when BOTH the ERROR phrase and a value are written - 'GOBACK WITH ERROR STATUS 0.' cannot both indicate error and pass 0 through one channel. docs/CONFORMANCE.md items 192/193 publish the resolution (the VALUE wins whenever present; ERROR/NORMAL supplies 1/0 only when it is absent), it was surveyed against GnuCOBOL 3.2 before being kept (kb/Work PB169), and GR7's own 'if such a capability exists within the operating system' is the latitude it rests on.
